sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce users/groups and account access via permission sets with temporary sessions; root credentials are reserved for rare root-only tasks, and IAM users have long-term credentials.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Create an IAM user in every account and distribute access keys to the directory groups.
Use IAM Identity Center with the directory, assign groups to accounts through permission sets, and let users obtain temporary sessions.
Create one root user per employee and require MFA for each account.
Store staff passwords in Secrets Manager and have employees assume one shared administrator role.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: A VPC endpoint policy narrows requests through the endpoint but does not replace identity/resource policies; an S3 bucket policy can enforce a specific endpoint path; gateway endpoints use route tables and S3 prefix-list network rules.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Restrict the S3 gateway endpoint policy to the required bucket and actions.
Add a bucket policy that denies requests unless they use the designated VPC endpoint.
Add a NAT gateway and allow the application role to call any S3 bucket.
Use a security group rule to restrict the bucket to the VPC endpoint ID.
Enable S3 default encryption and rely on encryption to block requests from other networks.

sourceVerification.method: Official AWS documentation opened with the web documentation reader; direct shell requests are still blocked by HTTP tunnel 403.
sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Secrets Manager supports runtime secret retrieval and automatic rotation; roles provide temporary credentials; Parameter Store is a separate parameter store choice and does not supply Secrets Manager rotation semantics by itself.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Put the password in an environment variable and rotate it manually during deployments.
Store the credential in AWS Secrets Manager, configure supported rotation, and have the workload role retrieve the current secret at runtime.
Store it in an SSM Parameter Store SecureString and retrieve it with a role, but rely on a separate manual process to rotate it.
Use an IAM permissions boundary because it encrypts database credentials.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec tunnels over internet connectivity and provides two tunnels; Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection and is unnecessary when rapid, moderate variable traffic is the stated constraint.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: AWS Site-to-Site VPN, with both provided IPsec tunnels configured for redundancy.
A dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection as the only path; it can be established immediately without a provider or cross-connect.
VPC peering over the public internet, with TLS enabled on application requests.
An internet gateway attached to the VPC, with inbound security group rules for the data center.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Cross-account SSE-KMS reads require both S3 authorization and KMS key authorization, including an appropriate key policy and caller permissions.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Grant s3:GetObject in the bucket policy; S3 object permission alone is sufficient to decrypt SSE-KMS data cross-account.
Permit the partner account or role to use the customer-managed KMS key in the key policy, and grant the partner role the required KMS permission as well as S3 read access.
Share the AWS-managed aws/s3 key with the partner account by adding a key policy statement.
Make the bucket public and rely on the KMS key to identify the intended partner.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: ECS target tracking can use SQS backlog per task; queue depth metrics reflect waiting work, while CPU alone can miss a backlog when tasks are I/O bound.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Scale only on average CPU utilization.
Scale on visible messages per running task, using queue depth divided by the number of active tasks.
Scale on the number of messages already in flight, without considering visible backlog.
Increase the task memory limit whenever the queue depth rises.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: API Gateway REST API stage/method cache settings can cache configured responses; scope cache use to shared responses and protect private/customer-specific variants with suitable cache-key behavior or no cache.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Enable API Gateway response caching only on the shared catalog routes with a short suitable TTL; leave personalized routes uncached.
Cache all API responses under a single cache key so every route has the highest hit rate.
Increase the database writer size and cache no responses, even for identical public catalog reads.
Move the entire API to an SQS queue so each client polls until its read response is available.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: AWS service quotas constrain capacity; AWS reliability guidance recommends managing quotas across accounts/Regions and testing disaster-recovery procedures.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Raise or validate the required service quotas in the recovery Region and regularly test the failover and scale-up procedure.
Assume quotas are global because the application uses the same AWS account in both Regions.
Remove the standby and rely on backups; that makes the current recovery-time target automatic.
Reduce the primary Region’s quotas so the standby Region receives capacity.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: RDS Proxy pools/manages client database connections and can improve failover behavior; compatibility and transaction behavior still require application validation.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Place RDS Proxy between the application and database and validate the application’s driver and transaction behavior.
Add an RDS read replica and send all write transactions to it during failover.
Put an S3 gateway endpoint between the application and database.
Replace the database with an EC2 instance in one Availability Zone.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: EBS Multi-Attach supports specified io1/io2 configurations and instance/zone constraints; a cluster-aware filesystem is needed for coordinated shared block access.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: An io2 EBS volume with Multi-Attach enabled, after confirming the Region, instance, and filesystem support requirements.
A gp3 EBS volume attached to several instances using ordinary filesystem mounts with no cluster coordination.
An S3 bucket mounted as a POSIX block device with simultaneous write locking.
An EFS file system, because it exposes the same shared block device to each instance.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Lambda CPU allocation increases in proportion to configured memory; benchmark representative duration and cost for a CPU-bound function.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Increase the function’s memory setting and benchmark duration and cost, because Lambda allocates CPU in proportion to configured memory.
Increase the function timeout; this allocates more CPU to each invocation.
Attach a larger EBS volume; Lambda execution environments do not use EBS for function CPU allocation.
Increase reserved concurrency; this raises the CPU allocation of each individual invocation.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: A GSI can provide an alternate partition/sort key access pattern and GSI reads are eventually consistent; projected throughput/cardinality constraints matter.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Create a global secondary index with status as its partition key and time as its sort key, then query that index.
Run a strongly consistent Scan on the base table and discard records that do not match.
Create a local secondary index whose partition key is different from the table partition key.
Add a read replica to the DynamoDB table.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: S3 storage classes and lifecycle rules support archival transitions; Glacier Flexible Retrieval restore times and charges/minimum duration must be considered for infrequent, delayed access.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, while accounting for the class’s minimum storage duration and retrieval charges.
S3 Standard, because it has the lowest storage price for data that is rarely accessed.
S3 Express One Zone, because it is designed for long-term archival with hours-long retrieval.
Delete the reports after 60 days, because lifecycle rules cannot retain objects in archival classes.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Compute Savings Plans apply across EC2 instance families and Regions and also Fargate/Lambda; Capacity Reservations solve capacity reservation rather than the stated broad compute-spend flexibility.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: A Compute Savings Plan, after validating that the committed hourly amount fits the organization’s steady usage.
An EC2 Instance Savings Plan tied to one instance family and Region.
Spot Instances for all customer-facing baseline capacity, without an interruption strategy.
On-Demand Capacity Reservations, because they automatically provide a billing discount.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: ElastiCache can cache repeated database query results; TTL/invalidation and hit-rate/freshness/cost tradeoffs determine fit.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Add a cache such as ElastiCache for the repeated catalog reads, with an explicit TTL or invalidation strategy and a cost/ hit-rate review.
Add a database read replica but send every request to both the primary and replica.
Disable database backups so fewer reads are billed.
Move the catalog to a larger database instance before measuring whether repeated reads can be served from a cache.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: NAT gateways are zonal and charged by gateway-hour/data processed; per-AZ local routing removes an egress dependency on another AZ, with cross-AZ transfer costs included in the design tradeoff.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each zone’s private subnets to its local gateway, accepting the additional gateway-hour cost.
Keep one NAT gateway in one Availability Zone and route both zones through it because this always has the lowest total cost and no availability tradeoff.
Replace NAT gateways with an internet gateway and assign public IPv4 addresses to all application instances.
Route all traffic through a Transit Gateway; it removes NAT processing charges and guarantees lower cost.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is intended for unknown/changing access patterns, has a monitoring/automation charge, and automatic tiers preserve millisecond access; asynchronous archive tiers require restore.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering and include its per-object monitoring and automation charge in the cost model.
Transition every object to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 30 days, regardless of access.
Keep all objects in S3 Standard because changing access patterns make tiering impossible.
Move the objects to S3 One Zone-IA and accept retrieval latency and single-AZ storage risk.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Requester Pays moves request and download data-transfer charges to authenticated requesters who signal acceptance; bucket owner continues to pay storage.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Enable Requester Pays and require consumers to make authenticated requests that acknowledge requester billing.
Apply a bucket lifecycle rule that transitions objects to S3 Standard-IA.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and leave all request charges with the bucket owner.
Use S3 Storage Lens to assign each consumer’s data transfer charges to their account.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Scheduled EC2 Auto Scaling actions adjust capacity for predictable time windows; lowering minimum/desired capacity outside the window removes idle instances when no work is needed.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Create scheduled scaling actions to raise capacity before the work window and reduce the group’s minimum and desired capacity after it.
Keep the group at its current size and purchase a one-year Compute Savings Plan.
Replace the group with a larger instance so tasks finish sooner during the same operating hours.
Add a target-tracking policy that scales out when CPU is low.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: Compute Optimizer presents Graviton price/performance comparisons, not an application compatibility guarantee; architecture-specific binaries must be tested and benchmarked before deployment. This is a validation decision, not a claim that every workload will save money.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Validate ARM64 support across binaries, libraries, and images, then benchmark representative workloads and compare projected and observed cost and performance.
Switch every instance immediately because a Graviton recommendation guarantees compatibility and lower total cost.
Purchase Reserved Instances for the existing x86 family; this verifies whether the application can run on ARM64.
Move the service to Spot Instances because CPU utilization is steady and high.

sourceVerification.qualification: The recommendation is a candidate for measured compatibility/performance testing, not a guarantee of application compatibility or savings.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: DynamoDB provisioned capacity charges for provisioned units; auto scaling can respond to workload changes and reduce unused provisioned capacity, while on-demand is request-based and avoids provisioned-capacity planning.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Provisioned capacity with Application Auto Scaling policies, validated against observed peaks and required headroom.
On-demand capacity permanently, because it is always less expensive when usage is predictable.
A global secondary index for every attribute so DynamoDB can allocate capacity automatically.
Replace DynamoDB with an RDS read replica, preserving the same key-value access pattern.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: DynamoDB Standard-IA offers lower storage cost and higher request cost; total suitability depends on observed storage/throughput mix.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Test the DynamoDB Standard-IA table class and compare lower storage charges against its higher request charges for this workload.
Move all items to DynamoDB Standard because that table class always has the lowest storage price.
Switch from provisioned to on-demand capacity; capacity mode automatically reduces table storage charges.
Export the records to S3 Glacier Deep Archive and continue querying them with DynamoDB Query at the same latency.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: VPC peering has no connection creation charge but cross-AZ/Region data transfer charges may apply; Transit Gateway charges attachment hours and data processing.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: VPC peering between the required pairs, while including applicable data-transfer charges in the estimate.
A Transit Gateway with every VPC attached, because it has no hourly or data-processing charges.
A public NAT gateway in each VPC for private VPC-to-VPC traffic.
AWS Direct Connect between the VPCs, because it removes all inter-VPC transfer charges.

sourceVerification.verifiedClaim: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints have no additional endpoint charge; NAT pricing includes hourly and data-processing charges, and AZ-local paths avoid routing egress through another zone when the measured savings justify an extra gateway.

optionExplanationsChecked.choice: Add S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints and route their service traffic through the endpoints.
Place a NAT gateway in each AZ and route each private subnet through the NAT gateway in its own AZ.
Route both AZs through one NAT gateway in the first AZ to avoid paying for a second gateway.
Send S3 and DynamoDB requests through the public internet and a NAT gateway because gateway endpoints add a per-hour charge.
Replace all private subnet routes with a single cross-Region Transit Gateway attachment.

Spot Instances
